title: Rio Tinto releases second quarter 2026 production results
body_text: Driving performance to achieve 3% YoY CuEq1 growth in the first half MELBOURNE, Australia--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Rio Tinto Chief Executive Simon Trott said: "We are delivering growth as we drive performance across the group, with copper equivalent production up 3 per cent in the first half. “Our scale, geographical diversification and sophisticated supply chains continue to underpin our resilience and strong operational performance despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainty throughout the period. “In the Pilbara, we achieved our highest first half iron ore production since we set a record in 2018, through the successful implementation of our ongoing productivity improvement program. In copper, Oyu Tolgoi continued to ramp up on schedule to deliver more than 30 per cent growth for the first half, while our integrated, large-scale aluminium business sustained its strong performance. “At Simandou, we continue to advance at pace. SimFer mine construction and port infrastructure are both now more than three quarters complete, with full rail commissioning achieved in the first quarter. We are progressing our next generation of copper growth options at Resolution and Winu, while in lithium we achieved first production ahead of plan at Sal de Vida and Fénix 1B. “We are driving a step-change in operational performance to deliver industry leading returns and growth for our shareholders." Executive Summary Operational excellence: 3% YoY increase in copper equivalent (CuEq)1 production for the first half. Copper: Oyu Tolgoi ramp-up remains on track; H1 production delivered 31% YoY growth. Copper C1 net unit cost guidance has been reduced to US 30 - 50c/lb (from US 65 - 75c/lb). Iron ore: Q2 global iron ore sales were 89Mt, up 5% YoY. Q2 Pilbara sales up 7% YoY. SimFer mine construction and port infrastructure now both over three quarters complete. Aluminium: Resilience across the supply chain, with a strong recovery in bauxite. Lithium: Production rose 20% YoY in Q2 driven by the ramp-up at Rincon starter plant and delivery of first tonnes at Sal de Vida and Fénix 1B, ahead of plan. title: AI for Recruitment Efficiency: 10 Ways to Streamline Your Hiring Process
summary: Discover how AI automates 80% of recruiting tasks. Learn 10 proven ways to reduce admin burden, scale interviews 24/7, and boost recruiter productivity with Alex.
body_text: Your recruiters spend the majority of their time on administrative tasks: scheduling interviews, updating your Applicant Tracking System (ATS), and chasing responses. Alex transforms this reality by automating these workflows, freeing your team for strategic work that closes placements. Here's what you'll learn in this article: How AI eliminates resume screening bottlenecks and surfaces qualified candidates from hundreds of applications Why structured interviews deliver 23% better reliability than unstructured processes How automated workflows free recruiters from administrative tasks to focus on strategic hiring How Verify protects hiring integrity against modern candidate fraud How to rediscover silver-medalist candidates already in your ATS before spending on job boards These strategies work together to help recruiting teams achieve the 80/20 flip: moving from 80% admin work to 80% strategic, revenue-generating activities. 1. Eliminate Resume Screening Bottlenecks When applications flood in by the hundreds, recruiters face an impossible choice: spend hours reviewing every resume or risk missing qualified candidates entirely. Manual screening creates operational bottlenecks that slow time-to-hire and frustrate hiring managers waiting for qualified shortlists. Resume Screens evaluates every incoming application with transparent scoring and structured rationale, so recruiters know exactly why a candidate was recommended or flagged. For candidates who advance, AI Interviews conducts structured conversations with every candidate rather than requiring manual phone screens. The platform conducts 5,000+ interviews daily, ensuring 100% candidate coverage with consistent evaluation. Organizations implementing AI-powered recruitment screening report significant cost-per-hire reductions and time-to-hire improvements by eliminating the manual screening bottleneck entirely. After each interview, recruiters can use Ask Alex to instantly query interview transcripts and extract specific insights without reviewing full recordings. 2. Scale Technical Assessment with Structured Interviews Generalist recruiters struggle to evaluate technical candidates accurately, leading to unqualified candidates advancing while strong performers get filtered out. This assessment gap costs teams time, credibility with hiring managers, and ultimately placements. Structured interviews achieve 0.84 reliability coefficients compared to 0.68 for unstructured formats, about 20–25% improvement in measurement consistency. AI Interviews applies this structured approach at scale, giving every candidate identical assessment standards through adaptive follow-up questions and transparent 100-point scoring. Implementation requires proper validation per EEOC guidance: employers must verify AI tools are job-related and conduct regular fairness testing, as bias in AI employment falls under EEOC enforcement priorities. 3. Enable 24/7 Candidate Screening Across Time Zones Top candidates often can't accommodate daytime interview availability. They're working, traveling, or managing personal commitments during business hours. Traditional recruiting constrains scheduling to when your team is online, which means losing qualified candidates to faster competitors. AI Interviews operates continuously across 26+ languages, conducting 5,000+ candidate conversations daily. With 48% of interviews completed after hours, candidates advance through your pipeline while your team sleeps. Candidates frequently describe AI Interviews' conversations as fair and surprisingly human . For staffing firms managing 10-15 recruiters, this capacity multiplication directly impacts revenue per recruiter. Human recruiters max out at approximately 16 interviews per day. AI-powered recruitment tools enable firms to scale placement volume without proportionally increasing headcount, breaking the linear relationship between revenue growth and team size. 4. Standardize Evaluation with Consistent Scoring Inconsistent interview processes produce unpredictable results. One hiring manager asks tough questions while another keeps it conversational. Strong candidates get rejected by rigorous interviewers while weak candidates advance through lenient ones. This variability undermines hiring quality and creates legal exposure. AI Interviews delivers standardized assessments across roles, hiring managers, and timing, ensuring consistent follow-up depth and scoring. Every candidate receives the same evaluation rigor through the platform's 100-point scoring system, which produces clear, objective results that hiring managers can compare directly. This consistency helps organizations build more equitable hiring processes while improving the quality of hire. 5. Automate Interview Scheduling and Recruiting Workflows Your recruiters spend hours each week playing email tag: coordinating availability across candidates, interviewers, and conference rooms. This administrative busywork doesn't advance a single placement, yet it consumes time that should go toward client relationships and strategic hiring decisions. Coordinator orchestrates this coordination automatically. When AI Interviews completes a candidate screening, Coordinator syncs results to your ATS, updates candidate status, notifies hiring managers, and triggers next-step workflows. The platform provides bi-directional synchronization with Workday, SuccessFactors, Greenhouse, Lever, Bullhorn, and other major ATS platforms. High administrative burden directly impacts recruiting performance through longer time-to-fill, lower recruiter satisfaction, and increased cost-per-hire. Coordinator eliminates these friction points by automating recruiting workflows end-to-end. 6. Automate Candidate Communication with Triggered Workflows Candidates drop out when they feel ignored. Every day without communication increases the likelihood they'll accept another offer or lose interest entirely. Yet maintaining consistent touchpoints across hundreds of candidates overwhelms recruiting teams already stretched thin. Coordinator handles automated candidate outreach through your workflows: application confirmations, interview invitations, status updates, and next-step communications. This consistent touchpoint cadence maintains candidate engagement without adding to recruiter workload. AI-powered communication drives candidate loyalty significantly. Candidates identify speed, personalization, and consistent updates as key benefits. When recruiters reduce administrative burden, they can dedicate more time to revenue-generating activities: building client relationships, negotiating offers, and closing candidates. 7. Deploy Multi-Signal Fraud Detection Candidate fraud has evolved beyond resume embellishment. Today's candidates use AI tools to generate polished interview responses, hire proxy interviewers, and manipulate video backgrounds. When fraudulent candidates reach client presentations or final rounds, they damage relationships and waste everyone's time. 91% of U.S. hiring managers have caught or suspected AI-driven candidate misrepresentation. The most common fraud tactics include fake voices and backgrounds (32%), AI scripts during interviews (32%), and deepfakes (18%). Only 60% of companies conduct identity checks as part of pre-employment screening, creating significant liability exposure. Verify addresses modern fraud patterns through multi-signal analysis: AI-generated response detection, identity verification, behavioral anomaly detection, and IP/location mismatch flagging. Unlike one-way video tools that candidates easily game, Verify works in real-time during two-way conversations, catching identity fraud before candidates advance. 8. Implement Enterprise-Grade Identity Verification Enterprise procurement teams require security credentials before approving new vendors. Without proper certifications, recruiting platforms create compliance gaps that put organizations at risk during audits and due diligence reviews. Verify confirms candidate identity through multi-signal verification and comprehensive audit logging. The platform maintains SOC 2 Type II certification with ISO 27001 compliance and GDPR alignment. Alex supports SAML 2.0 SSO and provides detailed audit trails for enterprise compliance requirements. For regulated industries and enterprise environments, these certifications demonstrate Alex AI's commitment to protecting sensitive candidate and client data throughout the hiring process. 9. Rediscover Silver-Medalist Candidates with ATS Mining You're spending thousands on job boards every month while qualified candidates who already interviewed with you sit forgotten in your ATS. These silver-medalist candidates, strong fits for previous roles who didn't quite make the final rounds, represent pre-screened talent you've already invested in sourcing. Talent Match uses natural language search to identify qualified candidates from existing ATS databases before pursuing external sourcing. Ask Talent Match to "show me all software engineers in New York who have a fintech background and speak Spanish" and get results that understand intent, not just keywords. Talent Match turns your ATS from a filing cabinet into an active talent pipeline, automatically surfacing candidates you've already vetted when new roles open. Internal sourcing consistently ranks among the most cost-effective recruitment channels , and Talent Match maximizes your return on previous sourcing investments. 10. Generate Automated Candidate-to-Role Matching Your ATS contains thousands of candidates, but finding the right ones for each new requisition requires manual searching that consumes valuable recruiter time. Meanwhile, qualified candidates sit uncontacted while recruiters work through backlogs. Talent Match automatically recommends qualified individuals for open positions based on skills, experience, and interview performance history. The platform surfaces candidates who interviewed well for related positions, even if they weren't selected, and identifies alternative roles where near-miss candidates with strong performance indicators might excel. When you combine faster screening through AI Interviews with proactive internal sourcing through Talent Match, you simultaneously reduce time-to-fill and external sourcing costs, achieving measurable improvements across key recruiting metrics . Scale Your Recruiting with Alex The fundamental recruiting challenge hasn't changed: evaluate more candidates faster while maintaining quality. What has changed is the availability of AI-powered products that handle the repetitive work, screening, scheduling, verification, and sourcing, so your team focuses on strategic activities that close placements. Alex integrates with your existing ATS through SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified infrastructure. Organizations adopting Alex as their AI recruiting platform achieve measurable improvements in cost-per-hire, time-to-hire, and recruiter productivity. title: AI Spatial Assist makes BIM accessible to every construction stakeholder
body_text: Today we're excited to announce the launch of AI Spatial Assist , a new AI capability that allows anyone, regardless of BIM expertise, to instantly navigate, interrogate, and review complex building models using natural language. Available across Resolve's high-performance web viewer and immersive VR environment, AI Spatial Assist enables teams to ask questions, locate equipment, teleport to rooms, and navigate models in seconds without relying on technical specialists or complex software interfaces. The launch addresses one of construction's most persistent productivity drains: the time it takes to find and validate project information. Industry research shows project teams spend roughly 20% of the time in meetings or long communication threads and another 14% tracking down information each week. A significant portion of that time is spent doing model reviews, scheduling coordination sessions, screen-sharing navigation, and relying on BIM specialists to retrieve answers locked inside complex 3D environments. Yet despite this massive coordination investment, many projects still suffer costly downstream rework. When operability constraints, installation conflicts, or access issues go unnoticed during design, they surface later during procurement, installation, or commissioning. And at a time where the demands for AI infrastructure are higher than ever, the industry cannot afford these delays. Eliminating the BIM Bottleneck Historically, BIM review has depended on BIM/VDC specialists to operate software, navigate geometry, and extract insights. This created an operational bottleneck where subject matter experts, from facilities leaders to field teams, can't easily validate design models on their own. AI Spatial Assist removes that dependency and frees up VDC teams for higher impact work. Users can simply ask: "Take me to the electrical room on Level 2." "Where are the cooling towers located?" "Which P&ID is this valve a part of?" The AI agent understands BIM geometry and metadata for seamless navigation and understanding of complex 3D models. If you've clicked on an object in the model, the agent will also use that context to answer questions like "what is this?" Improving Speed and Quality at the Same Time AI Spatial Assist is designed to improve both delivery velocity and quality simultaneously. By making BIM instantly accessible, the platform eliminates meetings whose sole purpose is navigating models or retrieving information. Subject matter experts can review directly, validate assumptions earlier, and flag risks without waiting on technical intermediaries. At the same time, broader participation leads to better outcomes. Facilities teams validate maintainability. Field leaders assess install risks. Operators confirm equipment access and safety, all before construction begins. Feedback cycles are compressed from weeks to minutes and deliverables are better aligned with the realities of construction and operations. Capturing What Rules-Based AI Misses Many emerging AI tools in design and construction focus on rules-based validation by checking models against documented requirements such as permitting regulations, building codes, and engineering standards. While critical, these systems operate on knowledge that is already written down. Some of construction's highest-value intelligence, however, is rarely formally documented. Operational feedback about maintainability, service access, installation practicality, and real-world usability lives primarily in the experience of facilities leaders, operators, and field teams. Historically, this expertise has been difficult to capture, easy to lose between projects, and rarely incorporated upstream into design. As the industry faces a growing labor shortage and generational workforce transition, preserving and scaling this knowledge is becoming increasingly urgent. By making BIM models instantly accessible through natural language, AI Spatial Assist enables these stakeholders to engage directly allowing teams to capture and structure feedback that would otherwise remain siloed or lost. The First Step Toward Compounding Intelligence Resolve positions AI Spatial Assist as the foundation of a broader vision. One where every project review strengthens the next. Each interaction generates structured insight: risks identified, access issues flagged, coordination conflicts surfaced, and operational feedback captured. Over time, this creates a growing intelligence layer across infrastructure portfolios. Resolve AI Spatial Assist is rolling out to select partners today and teams can sign up for the waitlist at https://www.resolvebim.com/ai

title: Duvet vs. Comforter: What Is a Duvet + Key Differences
summary: Discover the differences between a duvet and a comforter. Learn how each type of blanket works plus how to choose the right option for you.
body_text: Key Takeaways A duvet is a type of blanket utilizing a multi-layered fabric filled with stuffing made from natural or synthetic fibers. Duvet inserts go into a duvet cover for added warmth, comfort, and protection. A comforter is one piece of bedding made of a cloth exterior and filled with soft, synthetic fibers. The differences between duvets and comforters are that duvets have layers, require a duvet cover, and come in a variety of weights. With countless bedding options available, it's easy to get confused and difficult to know where to start. This blog provides you with a thorough look into two primary bedding options most considered by consumers. One of which is the duvet — a quilt filled with stuffing that adds comfiness, coziness, and warmth. This pillow-like filling typically consists of natural fibers like feathers, down, wool, or even synthetic alternatives, like microfiber or hollow fiber. The second choice is the comforter, a single piece of bedding that doesn’t require an outer shell or cover, like a duvet. Read on to learn everything you need to know about duvets and comforters, including their similarities and differences. Upgrade Your Sheets With Purple Purple SoftStretch® sheets are made with a soft, durable bamboo blend for maximum comfort. Shop Purple SoftStretch® Sheet Set What Is a Duvet Cover? A duvet cover is a protective layer for a duvet. It consists of two pieces of thin material sewn together with an opening at one end for inserting a duvet. They are easy to remove, store, and wash by machine. Using a duvet is easy: simply insert your duvet inside your duvet cover and seal up the open end, typically with buttons or a zipper. While it might seem like extra work compared to a blanket or comforter , this design has a purpose. A removable cover ensures the duvet stays clean, limits the need to wash the heavy duvet insert, and allows you to select an aesthetic cover of your choosing. In comparison, comforters, which are made from the same materials as a duvet insert, are not protected by a cover and require regular cleaning that oftentimes proves difficult. Duvet covers can be made from cotton, silk, bamboo fibers, flannel, or polyester. For a good night’s sleep, a breathable material is key. Our hypoallergenic PerfectStay™ Duvet Cover Set ensures optimal temperatures throughout the night by retaining heat when cool and releasing heat when warm. Benefits Considerations Soft and cozy because of inner stuffing Prone to sliding inside the duvet cover if not secured Easy to keep a duvet insert clean because an easily removable cover protects it Require a cover, often sold separately Simply change your bedding style by replacing the cover Can be a hassle to take most duvet covers off and put them on What Is a Duvet? A duvet is a plush, stuffed type of blanket that goes inside a duvet cover. Duvet inserts are sometimes called “down comforters.” Duvets, or “duvet inserts,” provide warmth, comfort, and ease of use. Unlike blankets, duvet inserts use stuffing materials like down feathers, wool, cotton, or polyester stuffing for added fluff and bulk that many sleepers find cozier. Keep in mind that stuffing materials will highly influence the price of your duvet. For example, down is generally the most expensive stuffing, but it can provide added comfort and breathability. Purple’s TempBalance™ Duvet uses a hypoallergenic down alternative. You can sleep comfortably all year round with this temperature-regulating duvet. Our quilted design keeps the duvet filling in place, so the typical annoyance of duvet movement is not a concern. What Is a Comforter? A comforter is a single piece of bedding that goes over your sheets. The typical comforter is a blanket consisting of a cloth exterior filled with soft, synthetic fibers. It typically serves as the top layer of bedding over your sheets. Available in a variety of sizes and thread counts , comforters offer ample range for creating your bedding aesthetic. Benefits Considerations You only need to buy one piece Can be hot and stuffy on warmer nights Easier to store than duvets More effort to clean Often comes in a set with matching sheets and bedding No option to change the cover if there’s a spill or stain The filling is consistently distributed for predictable coverage Differences Between Duvet and Comforter The main difference between duvets and comforters is that duvets use a cover and comforters do not. Comforters use the same materials as a duvet, but duvets are thicker than comforters. Retailers sometimes use “comforter” for “duvet” and vice versa, which can prove confusing. While duvets may require more pieces than a comforter, their design can save you time as they are easier to clean due to their removable covers. With a duvet, you simply remove the cover and wash it, whereas comforters are full of materials, so washing them can be time-consuming and problematic. Duvet Cover Size vs. Comforter Size While duvets appear fuller on your bed, they actually tend to be slightly smaller than comforters, providing a “flush” fit. In comparison, comforters are designed to hang over the sides of your bed slightly. Both duvets and comforters are available in every mattress size . Use the table below to better understand duvet and comforter standard sizes : Size Duvet Comforter Twin/Twin XL 90" x 66" 86" x 66" to 88”x 86” Full/Queen 90" x 90" 96" x 86" to 100” x 88” King/Cal King 104" x 90" 102" x 86" to 107” x 96” Sizes for duvets and comforters can vary slightly based on manufacturers. Many manufacturers size up or down from the norm by a few inches so be sure to confirm sizes per option. It’s also important to know your mattress size when selecting bedding. If you have a thicker mattress , opt for a larger duvet or comforter to ensure proper coverage around the edges. How To Choose The Right Duvet vs. Comforter There are a variety of options for duvets and comforters, which all satisfy different wants and needs. Your final choice needs to suit your particular sleeping style and preferences. Use this guide to choose the right duvet or comforter for you. 1. Material Stuffing material is a crucial factor, especially if you want to use your duvet or comforter year-round. For example, hot sleepers might prefer a down alternative as this material is more temperature-regulating, while cold sleepers might prefer down. The primary choices for duvet insert or comforter filling include: Down alternative (usually a polyester material): comfy, durable, temperature-regulating, easy to wash Down: fluffy, comfy, some are machine-washable Down and feather blend: fluffy, comfy, some are machine-washable Wool: breathable, soft, some are machine-washable Polyester: less breathable, more durable, easy to wash 2. Size To determine your blanket’s size , measure your bed. Your duvet insert or comforter should be larger than your bed’s dimensions. Manufacturers may use “queen size” to describe their duvet inserts, but it’s not always consistent between brands. First, ensure your blanket is longer and wider than your mattress. Then, consider your mattress height and how you want to style your bed. A properly sized duvet or comforter should cover the sides of your mattress without touching the floor. 3. Warmth You may have seen “fill weight” and “fill power” used to describe down or other types of filling. A fill power score indicates how fluffy a down filling is on a scale of 300-900, with 900 being the highest quality. A high number means high-quality insulation, with 600 and upwards typically denoting a high-quality option. Fill weight tells you how heavy a down filling is, but it’s less reliable for measuring warmth. You can use fill weight to find your preferred density, but fill power is better for determining the quality of a blanket’s insulation. A high-quality filling lets you enjoy a duvet or comforter year-round. Purple’s TempBalance™ Duvet uses a special temperature-regulating material for this purpose. Our down alternative provides all the comfort and convenience you need for a good night’s sleep. 4. Convenience Those who dislike the process of properly inserting a duvet into its insert may find using a comforter more convenient. However, you’ll have to use a top sheet with a comforter to avoid washing a comforter as often. Additionally, if you want to switch your comforter seasonally or for aesthetic reasons, you’ll need more storage space than you would with duvet covers. Duvet covers and inserts have a reputation for moving around, but this shouldn’t happen if you secure them. The best duvet inserts allow you to secure the duvet covers and inserts at each corner. The common options for securing duvets are: Ties Clips Loops Metal or plastic clips are easy enough to secure, but they can be bulky due to their material. Most duvets come with ties or loops, but this varies by brand. Purple’s soft-touch Velcro is the best of both worlds. Soft-touch Velcro keeps your duvet insert from moving without the need for bulky clips or fussy ties. 5. Cost Duvet inserts can cost anywhere from $50-$1,000, depending on the filling materials, fill weight, size, and brand. Pricier inserts use down, while less expensive options usually use synthetic materials, like polyester. Purple’s duvet inserts range from $229 for a twin/twin XL size to $279 for a king/California king. Every insert uses our down alternative for superior comfort at a friendlier cost. Comforters may be a bit more expensive, ranging from $30 to over $500. However, you’ll have to replace the entire item instead of just the duvet cover if it gets damaged or stained. 6. Cleaning When it comes to duvet vs. comforter care, the duvet takes top place for ease of cleaning. A duvet cover eliminates the need to wash the bulky duvet insert. The cover is easy to remove and wash making maintenance of your bedding much more effortless. By contrast, a comforter requires additional cleaning since it doesn’t have a protective cover. Getting a bulky comforter into a washing machine can be a Herculean task, most often requiring a trip to the dry cleaners. Additionally, replacing a duvet cover is much easier than replacing an entire comforter. Shop Bedding What Is the Best Duvet Insert for Hot Sleepers? The best duvet insert for hot sleepers is one filled with temperature-regulating stuffing. Down-stuffed inserts with a high fill power and low fill weight can provide comfort without trapping too much heat. Purple’s TempBalance™ Duvet is the perfect duvet insert for hot sleepers. title: Zoho alternatives: buy another CRM or build your own?
summary: Comparing Zoho alternatives? See how Airtable, Softr, monday.com, Glide, and Quickbase stack up against building a custom no-code CRM instead.
body_text: You didn't outgrow Zoho because it's a bad tool. You outgrew it because your firm's process doesn't fit neatly into anyone's template, and every workaround you've bolted on since setup has made the system a little harder to trust. So you start looking at Zoho alternatives. The problem is that most "alternatives" lists only offer you a different flavor of the same thing: another pre-built CRM with its own templates, its own pricing tiers, and its own version of the exact ceiling you just hit. There's a second option that rarely gets framed clearly: instead of buying another closed CRM, you build the one your firm actually needs on top of a no-code platform. This guide walks through both paths so you can tell which one actually solves your problem. TL;DR Zoho CRM is a capable, affordable platform, but customization, automation, and multi-user permissions get gated behind higher pricing tiers as your team grows. Off-the-shelf Zoho alternatives (other closed CRMs) fix pricing or interface complaints, but they come with the same structural limitation: you're still adapting your process to someone else's data model. No-code platforms like Airtable, Softr, monday.com, and Glide let you shape the CRM around your process instead, each with a different ceiling on permissions, client access, or workflow depth. Quickbase covers the enterprise end of that range, but it's built for IT-led teams, not a 10 to 50 person firm without a developer on staff. The real decision isn't "which CRM is best." It's "does another CRM fix what's actually broken, or is the real problem that no rigid template will ever fit." Why are service businesses looking for Zoho alternatives? Zoho CRM is priced reasonably at the entry level, and for a small team with a simple pipeline, it does the job. The friction shows up as firms grow: custom fields, advanced workflow automation, and multi-user portals live behind the Enterprise and Ultimate tiers, and pricing runs per user from roughly $14 to $52 a month depending on plan. That's a familiar shape. It's not that Zoho is uniquely restrictive, it's that any CRM built to serve thousands of different businesses has to draw its customization lines somewhere, and those lines rarely land exactly where your firm needs them. By 2025, 70% of new business applications used low-code or no-code technology, up from less than 25% in 2020, according to Gartner (2021) . A meaningful share of that shift is CRM, because customer data is exactly the kind of thing every firm structures a little differently. What's the real choice: another CRM, or a system you build yourself? Most "Zoho alternatives" content compares you to other closed CRMs: Pipedrive, HubSpot, Salesforce. Those are worth knowing about, but they solve a narrower problem than the one most operations leads are actually facing. If your complaint is "Zoho is too expensive for what we use," another CRM might fix that. If your complaint is "our process doesn't fit any CRM's default fields and stages," switching to a different closed tool usually just delays the same conversation by twelve months. No-code platforms answer a different question: instead of picking the CRM whose template happens to fit best, you define the fields, the stages, the permissions, and the automations yourself, on top of your own data. 71% of small businesses already use some form of CRM system , according to a 2024 Freshworks survey of 600 US business owners, which means most of this audience isn't choosing whether to use a CRM. They're choosing whether to keep renting someone else's structure or build their own. Here's how Zoho stacks up against the field, including the no-code route. Dimension Zoho CRM Airtable Softr monday.com Glide Quickbase Noloco Pricing model Per user, $14 to $52/mo depending on tier Per seat, plus per-editor Interface pricing Per seat Per seat, guest pricing for external users Per user, usage-based tiers Per seat, enterprise pricing Flat active-user pricing , no per-seat client fees Customization without code ⚠️ Gated by tier, deep customization needs Enterprise+ ✅ Strong on data structure ⚠️ Limited to pre-built blocks ⚠️ Board and template based ⚠️ Basic, limited backend logic ✅ Deep, but needs technical setup ✅ Full data model and workflow control Client-facing permissions ⚠️ Multi-user portals from Enterprise tier up ❌ Not built for client logins ⚠️ Page-level only ❌ Role-based only, paid guest seats ❌ Not built for client logins ✅ Yes, role-based ✅ Field and record-level permissions Where your data lives Zoho's own database Native spreadsheet-style database Connects to Airtable or Supabase Native database Connects to Airtable or Google Sheets Native, plus integrations Airtable , Noloco Tables, PostgreSQL, MySQL Best fit Simple pipeline, budget-conscious, no client access needed Teams that want structured data before adding a front end Quick client dashboards on existing Airtable data Familiar internal sales tracking Mobile-first field data, not full CRM IT-led enterprise deployments CRM, delivery, and client portal in one connected system ‍ When does building your own CRM make more sense than buying another one? Buying another CRM makes sense when your process is genuinely standard: a simple sales pipeline, a handful of stages, no client-facing access required. In that case, the fastest fix is often just picking a cheaper or simpler off-the-shelf tool. Building makes more sense once any of these are true: Your pipeline needs to connect to delivery, invoicing, or a client portal, not just sit as a standalone sales tool. Clients or external partners need to log in and see only their own records, not a shared view with everyone else's data. You've already tried two CRMs and hit the same customization ceiling both times. Your team is spending real time each week working around the tool instead of in it. That last point matters more than it sounds. A rigid CRM doesn't just annoy your team, it quietly trains them to keep a shadow spreadsheet next to it "just in case," which defeats the point of having a system of record at all. Stay on Zoho (or switch to another closed CRM) if Consider a no-code build instead if Your pipeline is simple: a handful of stages, no client access required Clients or partners need their own login showing only their records Your main complaint is price or interface, not structural fit Your CRM needs to connect directly to delivery, invoicing, or project tracking Your team hasn't hit a customization ceiling yet You've already switched CRMs once and hit the same wall again You want a system live in days with minimal setup Your team keeps a shadow spreadsheet next to the CRM to work around it You have no existing structured data to build from You're already on Airtable or Sheets and don't want to lose that data ‍ How do Airtable, Softr, monday.com, and Glide compare as Zoho alternatives? Airtable Airtable is the most common starting point for firms building their own CRM, and for good reason: linked records, custom fields, and views make it a genuinely flexible database. Many operations leads are already keeping some part of their business in an Airtable base. Where it stops being enough as a CRM on its own is client access. Airtable's sharing options are built for internal collaboration, not for giving a client a login that shows only their records. Firms that like their Airtable data usually keep it as the source of truth and add an interface layer on top rather than migrating away from it. Softr Softr turns an Airtable or Google Sheets base into a client-facing site or portal fast, which makes it a reasonable next step once Airtable alone isn't enough for client visibility. Pre-built blocks get a simple deal tracker with a client login running quickly. The tradeoff shows up as your process gets more complex. Permissions are managed page by page rather than at the data level, which gets harder to keep secure as your client list grows, and Softr pulls data live from the source on every page load, which can slow things down at scale. monday.com monday.com's CRM template is familiar and easy to sell internally, since most teams have already used its boards for project tracking. It handles an internal-only sales pipeline well. It wasn't built around external, client-facing use. Giving clients access typically means per-seat guest pricing, and permissions are role-based rather than field-level, so there's no clean way to let a client see some records but not others within the same view. Glide Glide is strong for fast, mobile-friendly apps on top of a spreadsheet or Airtable base, particularly for field teams who need a lightweight view on a phone. As a full CRM, it's a harder fit. Backend logic is limited, so multi-step workflows and more complex relational data tend to break down. It's a better match for simple record-and-view use cases than for a CRM tied into delivery and billing. Quickbase Quickbase sits at the enterprise end of this comparison: relational data, role-based permissions, and serious workflow automation, built for organizations with a dedicated IT function. For a 10 to 50 person service business without an in-house developer, that depth comes at a real cost. Implementation usually needs a consultant or technical lead, pricing is enterprise-tier, and the learning curve for non-technical operators is steep. It earns a place in this comparison because it comes up in searches, but it's rarely the right fit for this size of firm. Noloco Noloco takes a different position in this comparison: instead of a CRM template you customize within someone else's limits, it's an operating system for service businesses where your CRM, delivery tracking, and client portal all run on the same connected data. You can connect Noloco directly to an existing Airtable base, so nothing has to be re-entered, or build your data model from scratch inside Noloco. On top of that, field-level and record-level permissions mean your team and your clients can share the same system while seeing only what's relevant to them, and pricing is based on active users rather than per seat, so client access doesn't carry the same cost penalty it does with Zoho's guest-style pricing or per-seat competitors. That combination is what makes it worth considering alongside the "buy another CRM" option: instead of trading one set of limits for another, you're removing the ceiling entirely. How should you actually decide? Start by naming the specific thing that's broken. "Zoho feels expensive" and "Zoho can't model our delivery process" are different problems with different fixes, and it's worth being honest about which one you actually have before you evaluate anything. If it's genuinely a pricing or interface complaint and your process is simple, a cheaper off-the-shelf CRM may be the fastest fix. If it's a structural fit problem, no closed CRM, Zoho or otherwise, will solve it permanently. That's the signal to look at a no-code build instead. From there, match the tool to what's actually missing: Airtable if you need a better database and nothing else yet, Softr or monday.com if you need a simple client-facing layer on top of what you already have, and a connected system like Noloco if the CRM, delivery, and client access all need to work together without three separate subscriptions and a pile of Zapier automations holding them together. Final thoughts There's no universally right answer between buying another CRM and building your own. Both are legitimate paths, and the honest version of this decision depends entirely on how far off-template your actual process runs. What's worth avoiding is spending another year hopping between closed CRMs that each solve one complaint and introduce a new one. If you've already done that once, the pattern is unlikely to change the second time. Building on a flexible foundation, whether that's your existing Airtable data or a fresh system, tends to be the version of this decision that firms don't have to revisit again in twelve months. FAQ What's the main difference between a Zoho alternative and a no-code CRM? A Zoho alternative like Pipedrive or HubSpot is still a closed CRM with its own template and its own limits. A no-code CRM lets you define the fields, stages, permissions, and automations yourself, so the system follows your process instead of the other way around. Is it cheaper to switch CRMs or build one? It depends on your team size and process complexity. Switching CRMs usually has a lower upfront cost but risks hitting the same customization ceiling again. Building takes more setup time initially but tends to cost less over time once client access and automation needs grow. Can I keep my Zoho data if I move to a no-code platform? Yes, most no-code platforms support CSV import or direct integrations, and you're not required to migrate everything at once. Many firms start by exporting core records (contacts, deals) and rebuild workflows from there rather than a full one-time cutover. Do I need a developer to build my own CRM in a no-code tool? No. Platforms like Airtable, Softr, monday.com, and Noloco are built for non-technical teams using visual builders. Quickbase is the exception in this comparison; it's low-code and typically needs technical implementation support. Is Airtable a CRM on its own? Airtable can function as a basic CRM for internal pipeline tracking, but it lacks native client-facing permissions and portals. Most firms that build a CRM on Airtable add a front-end layer like Softr or Noloco on top to handle client access. What should I check before switching off Zoho? Map the specific limitation you've hit (pricing, customization, client access, automation) before comparing tools. This tells you whether another closed CRM will actually fix the problem, or whether you need a platform flexible enough to be shaped around your process instead. body_text: Recent Updates July 27, 2026 6:56 AM From AI arcades to robot demos: Inside Amazon's Kids Day From building AI-powered video games to cleaning up a miniature ocean, kids got hands-on with the technology shaping their future. Last week, more than 7,800 kids took over HQ1 in Seattle for the annual Bring Your Kids to Work Day, a two-day interactive experience designed to spark curiosity and creativity in the next generation of builders. What kids experienced at Amazon's Kids Day Across more than a dozen stations, kids explored everything from virtual reality training simulations to horticulture under a microscope. At the Agentic Arcade, built using AWS, kids answered questions that helped AI create a custom video game—then got to play it. At Badge in a Box, they designed their own AI-powered stickers. A highlight of the Seattle event: Lo-Fi Robotics Club, a local youth robotics club, partnered with Amazon to showcase their work alongside Amazon's Vulcan Robotics program. Kids also packed their own Amazon packages at the Pick and Pack station, used real stethoscopes at the Doctor for a Day booth with One Medical, and learned about recycling through a game called Trashketball. How AI and robotics sparked curiosity "Kids go from 'I can't do this' to 'What else can I make it do?' the moment their code actually works," said Ojas Suley, Risk and Compliance Specialist at Amazon and coach for Lo-Fi Robotics Club. “Events like these plant seeds—you never know which kid walks away thinking, 'I could actually make this a career.'” "Learn and Be Curious" is one of Amazon's Leadership Principles—and this expo brought it to life for the youngest members of the Amazon family. Whether they were free-building with LEGOs alongside a professional artist constructing a mural of Rufus, or learning about Amazon's ocean cleanup initiatives, kids left with more than just swag. They left with a glimpse of what's possible. Activities ran July 23-24 at Amazon's Seattle headquarters, with a similar event taking place at HQ2 in Arlington, Virginia in June. Amazon invests to bring AI education to 500,000 students nationwide Through a partnership with Playlab AI, Amazon is helping educators and students across the U.S. gain hands-on experience with AI while participating in the White House Presidential AI Challenge. June 30, 2026 3:15 PM Bringing soccer’s biggest moment to Puget Sound communities As one of the biggest moments in sports plays out in our hometown, Amazon is partnering with cities, nonprofits, and community organizations to make sure the excitement reaches every neighborhood, not just the stadium. Amazon helps bring more than 1,400 young people to the matches Through a partnership between Amazon, the City of Seattle, and the Seattle local organizing committee, more than 1,400 young people and their caregivers are attending tournament matches this summer—a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for families across the region. A new year-round field for Marysville Earlier this summer, Strawberry Fields Athletic Complex in Marysville opened a new synthetic turf field—a project Amazon supported alongside city and community partners. The field gives the growing community a durable, year-round space for youth sports and gatherings, with ADA-accessible seating, drainage upgrades, walkways, and lighting for evening play. Neighborhood celebrations across the region Amazon is supporting community-led programming throughout the Puget Sound : Federal Way: brought watch parties, live music, soccer clinics, and family activities—a festival for fans of all ages to celebrate. Tukwila: Tukwila United is running youth soccer clinics, equipment giveaways, a "Tuk Cup" tournament, and esports competitions in one of the region's most diverse communities. Redmond: . Bellevue: Tournament activations through the Bellevue Downtown Association bring fans together at The Meadow on the Amazon campus. Getting fans there, hassle-free Amazon is offering free evening and weekend parking and running free shuttles to Seattle Stadium, making it easy for fans to enjoy the matches stress-free. It's a global moment, felt locally—in new fields, shared experiences, and stronger community ties across the region. 5 ways Amazon is investing in Washington Amazon's investments are boosting the Evergreen State's economy while creating opportunities for Washingtonians. June 19, 2026 4:14 PM Shellabrating five years of restoring Puget Sound's native oysters Volunteers stack bags of Pacific oyster shells to use for expanding Olympia oyster populations in Puget Sound. Photo credit: Alabastro Photography This month, Amazon marks a 5-year partnership with Puget Sound Restoration Fund (PSRF), a Washington nonprofit restoring marine habitat and native species in Puget Sound. How Amazon volunteers help restore native oysters in Puget Sound On June 17, Amazon volunteers headed to Samish Bay to work alongside PSRF scientists and Taylor Shellfish Farms to build habitats for native Olympia oysters, or “Olys”. Since 2022, Amazon has helped rebuild native oyster populations that once thrived throughout the region, offering financial and volunteer support to outplant millions of young oysters. This year, volunteers stacked hundreds of bags of Pacific oyster shell to expand Oly populations and cleaned shells for scientific monitoring throughout Puget Sound. Photo credit: Alabastro Photography Why native oysters matter for Puget Sound's marine ecosystem Each Oly can filter up to 5 gallons of water per day. Dense oyster beds serve as nurseries for marine species, including young salmon and crabs. After a century of decline from overharvest, pollution, and habitat loss, PSRF’s restoration work, supported by Amazon’s sustained contributions, helps reverse that trend. What partners say about Amazon's oyster restoration work “Amazon has been a great partner, providing consistent funding and dedicated volunteers who unfailingly dive in on the hands-on work of oyster restoration,” said Jodie Toft, executive director of PSRF. “They have helped us successfully jumpstart the Olympia oyster population in one of Washington’s original Oly strongholds—Samish Bay—with one of our closest partners, Taylor Shellfish Farms.” “It’s inspiring to see Amazon’s team return year after year,” said Bill Dewey, director of public affairs at Taylor Shellfish. “Their involvement shows that corporate partnerships can make a measurable difference for our marine ecosystems.” Oyster fun fact: The West Coast's only native oyster is the Olympia oyster ( Ostrea lurida ), or "Olys.” Most oysters farmed and eaten in Washington are Pacific oysters. Both are “true” oysters, which belong to a different family than “pearl oysters.” Yet, on rare occasions, small pearls are found in true oysters. How Amazon team members volunteer year-round to strengthen local communities From supporting local food banks to delivering emergency supplies after disasters, Amazon volunteers connect with causes that matter to them year-round. June 5, 2026 3:12 PM Amazon unveils Whale Tail Selfless Station on Seattle campus Amazon Whale Tail selfless station unveiling. Andrew Devore (Amazon). Photo by Alabastro Photography. This summer, the world is coming to Seattle—and Amazon is welcoming them with public art rooted in the culture and community of the Pacific Northwest . On June 4, Amazon unveiled its Whale Tail Selfless Station on the Day 1 Playfield—one of 26 art pieces that are part of the Seattle Unity Loop. The Selfless Stations are large-scale public art and community engagement hubs where visitors can take photos, learn about local nonprofits, and donate to causes that matter. Amazon's whale tail was designed by Felicia "Felix" Bryan, an enrolled Chinook artist and scholarship recipient at Gage Academy of Art—one of Amazon's tenants on its Seattle campus. Raised in a family of artists, Felicia works across oil, beadwork, and block printing to tell stories of emotion, cultural heritage, and life experience. Their piece depicts the great blue heron (sbəq̓ʷaʔ), honoring Coast Salish spiritual traditions and the enduring connection between the natural and spiritual worlds. “To me, the blue heron represents not only a culturally significant bird, but a local icon found all along the Salish coast,” said Bryan. “Merging two iconic silhouettes together that, to me, represent Seattle the best, nature and culture, water and heritage.” The installation is part of Amazon's broader commitment to supporting Seattle communities this summer. Amazon is donating sports equipment to local organizations, sponsoring community games and clinics for families, and continuing to offer free public parking on evenings and weekends with free shuttle service to the stadium—making it easier for fans to get to games and encouraging the use of public transportation. The Whale Tail Selfless Station will remain on the Day 1 Playfield through the duration of the World Cup, before being moved to its permanent location on campus. Visitors are encouraged to stop by, take a photo, and learn more about the local nonprofits the program supports. Amazon to provide 2,000 free rapid response technology systems that restore critical services in minutes Each system is portable enough for one person to carry and set up, now scaling 50x ahead of hurricane season. June 4, 2026 1:40 PM Volunteers roll up their sleeves for spring cleanups across the Puget Sound During May’s Global Month of Volunteering , that meant rolling up their sleeves in two busy downtown neighborhoods: Seattle’s historic Pioneer Square and downtown Bellevue. Together, local volunteers helped care for shared public spaces and keep these neighborhoods clean and welcoming. Volunteers give Pioneer Square a spring refresh In Pioneer Square, Amazon supported the 16th annual Pioneer Square Spring Clean, where more than 200 volunteers gathered in Occidental Square before heading out across the neighborhood. Amazon volunteers joined community partners, including the Alliance for Pioneer Square and Seattle City Council members Dionne Foster and Alexis Mercedes Rinck, to pick up litter, plant, weed, mulch, and refresh one of Seattle’s most historic districts. The cleanup came at an important time for Pioneer Square. The neighborhood is home to many arts organizations, small businesses, and public spaces that bring people together before games, concerts, and the popular First Thursday Art Walk. As Seattle prepares to welcome visitors for the world's biggest soccer event, efforts like Spring Clean help support the neighborhood’s momentum and make sure the district is ready to welcome people from near and far. Amazon teams join the city of Bellevue for a downtown cleanup In Bellevue, more than 90 Amazon employees joined the city of Bellevue for a Keep Bellevue Beautiful cleanup. Volunteers began at The Meadow, Amazon’s 1.75-acre public space, before supporting litter cleanup and beautification efforts nearby. Beryl Tomay, Amazon’s vice president of transportation, joined Bellevue Mayor Mo Malakoutian for the event. Amazon’s Keep Bellevue Beautiful effort is part of a broader commitment to helping ensure Bellevue’s green spaces remain clean, accessible, and inviting. From downtown Seattle to Bellevue, these cleanups show how acts of service can make a visible difference in the communities Amazon employees and customers call home. 7 ways Amazon’s global pro bono program is creating lasting community impact The 2025 Pro Bono Report showcases how Amazon teams are expanding our impact with innovative AI tools, professional expertise, and by partnering with organizations to create lasting impact in underserved communities. April 28, 2026 10:14 AM Amazon celebrates the opening of The Meadow at Bellevue 600 Art installation by Oliver Jeffers called The Moon, the Earth and Us—two hand-painted sculptures of the Moon and Earth, scaled and positioned to reflect their true size and distance from one another. On April 27, Amazon celebrated the official opening of The Meadow—a new 1.75-acre public open space in the heart of downtown Bellevue at the company’s newest tower, the Bellevue 600 (B600) office development. Members of the Bellevue City Council, the city manager, city leadership staff, and community partners including the Bellevue Downtown Association joined Amazon for a ribbon-cutting ceremony. A space for art, nature, and community The Meadow is an open space built atop the future site of B600 Tower 2, designed to activate the site and welcome the community during interim development phases. The permanent portion of the space features an art installation by celebrated artist and children's book author Oliver Jeffers called The Moon, the Earth and Us —two hand-painted sculptures of the Moon and Earth, scaled and positioned to reflect their true size and distance from one another. Amazon acquired the piece last December and is giving it a permanent home in Bellevue. The urban meadow also features 100% native flowering plant species, designed to be a natural immersive garden with vibrant public spaces that is already providing habitat for native pollinators like birds and bees. Growing alongside Bellevue "Amazon's vision in Bellevue has always been to grow alongside this community," said Sean Lee, vice president of corporate real estate & facilities at Amazon. "Rather than closing off this site between development, we wanted to open it up—the Meadow gives the community a space to gather and enjoy right now. None of it is possible without the strong partnership we've built with the city of Bellevue and the community partners who help bring these spaces to life." Amazon has grown from 450 employees in Bellevue in 2017 to more than 15,000 today, making it the city's largest employer. B600 is Amazon's first self-developed project in Bellevue and a cornerstone of the Grand Connection. Amazon has also committed $22.6 million to local transportation projects and invested $100 million in affordable housing in Bellevue. Additionally, Amazon funds partnerships and projects across more than 80 organizations on the Eastside. Amazon commits over $70 million in scholarships to students across the US since 2019 Amazon has awarded 200 high school seniors with scholarships of up to $40,000 each, plus a paid internship opportunity at Amazon. April 17, 2026 10:39 AM Amazon and Inspire Washington launch digital passport to drive arts engagement Photo by Seattle Theater group Building on momentum from the winter months, Amazon is continuing its partnership with Inspire Washington through “Discover What Moves You,” a campaign focused on increasing attendance at arts, heritage, and science experiences across the Puget Sound. The Discover What Moves You Digital Passport is an extension of the campaign—a free, mobile experience that launched March 23. The passport lets users explore participating cultural organizations and small businesses, unlock discounts, and earn points toward prizes through May 31. Participating organizations span the region, from interactive spaces like KidsQuest Children’s Museum and Gage Academy of Art, to performance venues including Theatre33, STG at Kerry Hall, and the Seattle Symphony at Benaroya Hall. Institutions like the Northwest African American Museum, National Nordic Museum, Kirkland Arts Center, and BelRed Arts Studio are also part of the experience. Participating partners like the Northwest African American Museum see the program as an opportunity to reach new audiences. “The Discover What Moves You program is a meaningful example of how partnerships can expand access to arts, culture, and shared experiences,” said Brandon Bird, president and chief executive officer of the Northwest African American Museum. “By connecting people to the organizations that bring our stories to life, this initiative helps ensure our cultural ecosystem remains accessible, relevant, and deeply rooted in the communities we serve.” The program is designed to reduce barriers to participation at local cultural institutions. It emerged from conversations with partners about fluctuating attendance patterns throughout the year—an opportunity to help people stay connected to the arts and culture organizations that are essential to the fabric of the Puget Sound. Working with Inspire Washington, Amazon aimed to make it easier for individuals and families to discover everything from free events to performances and exhibits, while supporting the organizations that make this region a special place to live. April 13, 2026 11:39 AM Amazon's $7.5 million investment helps transform a 122-year-old railroad bridge into a trail for everyone A 122-year-old wooden railroad bridge in Bellevue, Washington, is getting a new life—and a new purpose. The Wilburton Trestle, a 975-foot-long, 102-foot-tall structure originally built in 1904 for the Northern Pacific Railway, is being reimagined as a community asset that connects housing, jobs, and transit across the Eastside and transformed into a centerpiece of the Eastrail regional trail. When it opens in summer 2027, visitors will walk or roll along an 18-foot-wide trail deck with three viewing platforms offering panoramic views of the Bellevue skyline, Lake Washington, and the Olympic Mountains. Amazon is helping to make it happen. In September 2021, the company committed $7.5 million to the project—$5 million for the Wilburton Trestle and $2.5 million for the adjacent Wilburton Trail Segment—closing the funding gap needed to begin construction. "Amazon is proud to partner with King County on this iconic project, transforming a unique piece of our regional history into a permanent community asset for everyone," said David Zapolsky , Amazon's chief global affairs and legal officer. "Strong public-private partnerships make projects like the Wilburton Trestle possible, and make our region a great place to live, work, and visit. We can't wait for this part of Eastrail to open and serve generations to come." King County Executive Girmay Zahilay recently led a hard-hat tour of the trestle alongside Zapolsky, King County Councilmember Claudia Balducci, Bellevue Deputy Mayor Dave Hamilton, and other regional partners to mark the project's progress. Amazon's investment in the Wilburton Trestle reflects the company's commitment to the communities where its employees live and work. title: AI Gun Detection for Schools: Top Solutions & Buying Guide
summary: AI gun detection alerts school security teams in real time. Compare leading solutions, understand accuracy benchmarks, and see implementation best practices.
body_text: Traditional cameras record incidents but rarely prevent them. AI gun detection for schools is changing that equation, applying computer vision and behavioral analysis to existing camera networks so threats surface in seconds, not after the SRO radio call. For school safety directors and district security leaders weighing how to modernize campus safety without replacing infrastructure, the starting point is understanding how this technology works and which approaches actually deliver early warnings before a lockdown. This guide explains core mechanics, proven accuracy rates, five leading school-ready platforms, and a practical deployment framework. What Is AI Gun Detection for Schools? AI gun detection software transforms the cameras you already own into weapon detection systems that spot a drawn firearm and alert responders within seconds. Traditional motion or metal detectors trigger only after a shot is fired or a checkpoint is breached, but intelligent video assessment software can identify threats before violence erupts. Unlike metal detectors at the front entrance, which can feel intrusive and turn the start of the school day into an airport-style screening line, AI gun detection works invisibly through the cameras already mounted in hallways and common areas. AI gun detection software overlays computer vision on your existing camera network to spot visible firearms, verify threats, and trigger lockdown procedures in seconds. The expectation is that detection happens before the first 911 call from a classroom or front office. By automating the most challenging aspect of surveillance, AI gun detection gives School Resource Officers and local first responders critical minutes that manual monitoring routinely loses. The software operates through three escalating levels of sophistication: Basic object recognition distinguishes handgun or rifle shapes from everyday objects like phone cases, laptop bags, or umbrellas, using multi-frame analysis Contextual understanding adds spatial awareness to detect threatening situations, like a firearm in a school hallway during passing period versus a baseball bat near the athletic fields Behavioral analysis monitors body language, crowd reactions, and movement patterns for early violence indicators, from fights in the cafeteria to a student concealing an object near a restricted entry AI weapons detection technology processes live video in real time through on-premises hardware or cloud services , where machine learning analyzes every frame. When threats are detected, the system can automatically send alerts to SRO radios, administrator phones, and front-office workstations, and deliver location-tagged images to first responders within seconds. High-severity alerts are typically verified by a human analyst before campus-wide notification to prevent unnecessary lockdowns and classroom disruptions. Educational campuses present unique challenges like dense foot traffic between bells, after-school events and night games that alter lighting conditions, and open quads where students carry sports equipment, instrument cases, and theater props that can resemble weapons. Continuous learning algorithms adapt to these variables while preserving privacy by ignoring faces and other personally identifiable student information. title: Partners Coffee Roasters introduces a new way to order and earn rewards with Per Diem
summary: Per Diem helps merchants grow with powerful mobile app solutions integrated seamlessly with Square.
body_text: ‍ Partners Coffee Roasters has brought its neighborhood café experience into a mobile app with help from Per Diem. The New York coffee company, which began in 2012 with a focus on great brews, community, and sustainable practices, has introduced a new ordering and loyalty app that carries its identity into the way guests order on their phones. The app is now available on the App Store and Google Play. ‍ Built with Per Diem and connected to Square point of sale, the Partners Coffee app lets guests order ahead, customize drinks, and earn rewards in a setting that feels familiar to regulars. The design and layout reflect the color, tone, and personality of the cafés so that the experience feels like Partners Coffee from the first screen to the pick-up counter. Customers can store credit, use coupons, and share referral rewards, all within a single branded space. For guests, the app turns everyday visits into a smoother routine. A regular can place a drink order on the way to the subway and find it ready when they arrive. Someone visiting a different Partners Coffee location can open the app, see the full menu, explore seasonal offerings, and start earning rewards from the first visit. Store credit and referral rewards give customers a straightforward way to keep value in their account and to invite friends into the brand. For the Partners Coffee team, the app offers a direct connection to their community without sending customers through third-party marketplaces. Orders flow into the existing Square setup, so staff see tickets in a format they already know. During busy mornings, mobile orders help spread out demand, shorten waits at the register, and give baristas more time to focus on drink quality and guest interaction. ‍ Partners Coffee has grown from a single roastery into a group of cafés that still feel closely tied to their neighborhoods. The choice to invest in a branded app reflects how guests now choose where and how to order, especially in a city where many people plan their coffee stop around a commute, a school drop off, or a meeting. With the new app, the company can offer the ease people expect while keeping the focus on its own coffee, its own spaces, and its own story. Per Diem builds mobile ordering and online ordering for cafés, bakeries, and restaurants that use Square POS. The company focuses on helping local merchants offer a clear and simple way for guests to order ahead, earn rewards, and pay online.
